answer: Sybil resistance here works by making identity expensive rather than free: every agent must post a bond held for many epochs and prove it owns a distinct network inlet, a unique egress path whose latency fingerprint is checked against three independent beacons. Faking a thousand bots then costs a thousand bonds plus bandwidth for a thousand separate paths, far more than running one honest node. On the frozen tundra testbed this made our small island of peers costly to flood and cheap to defend.
